title: Vidi Aquam (I Saw Water)
text:
I saw water proceeding out of the temple, from the right side, alleluia:
and all to whom that water came were saved, and they shall say: alleluia, alleluia.

Psalm 117:1
Give praise to the Lord, for he is good:
for his mercy endureth for ever.

Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.
As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

translation.latin:
Vidi aquam egredientem de templo, a latere dextro, alleluia:
et omnes ad quos pervenit aqua ista, salvi facti sunt, et dicent: alleluia, alleluia.

Confitemini Domino, quoniam bonus:
quoniam in saeculum misericordia ejus.

Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto.
Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Amen.

attribution: Based on Ezekiel 47:1-2 and Psalm 117:1 (Psalm 118:1 in Hebrew numbering)
notes: The Vidi Aquam replaces the Asperges Me during the Easter season, from Easter Sunday through Pentecost. It refers to the vision of Ezekiel where water flows from the Temple, prefiguring the sacraments and especially the grace of Baptism. The 'Alleluia' acclamations express the joy of Easter.
description: The Vidi Aquam is sung during the sprinkling of holy water in the Easter season
